title: How to Test International Payments on Your WooCommerce Store
summary: Test international payments on WooCommerce with Cashfree. Check foreign cards, multi-currency checkout, failed payments, refunds and webhooks before going live.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


WooCommerce enables you to accept international payments (“foreign” payments) when selling your products online from India. International payments enable you to accept money from customers in supported countries around the world. International payment options usually include foreign Visa/Mastercard credit/debit cards, wallets, and bank transfers, depending on the gateway and integration.


### Key Takeaways


- Foreign card acceptance does not require multi-currency checkout. You can accept supported foreign cards in INR.
- A currency converter can change displayed prices without changing the payment currency.
- Use matching sandbox credentials and test data, then verify order status, currency, failures, refunds and webhooks.
- Sandbox success does not establish live foreign-card acceptance or confirm a bank settlement.


##


Why Are International Payments Important for WooCommerce Stores?


- International payments make it possible to sell your products to a global marketplace.
- Digital products such as downloadable courses or software subscription services can be provided to a global marketplace.
- Expat users who have a preference to pay in INR (Indian rupee) can be supported.
- Corporate clients that are located outside of India can send you payment for your products/services.
- Your customers can purchase your product using their local currency if your checkout and payment gateway support it.


To establish international payments via WooCommerce, there are three main steps. The first step is to choose what currencies are available to your customers throughout WooCommerce. The second step is to decide which payment gateway will be used to facilitate international transactions. The final step is to fully test every aspect of your checkout process to ensure proper functionality.


##


WooCommerce Multi-Currency Payments: Display Currency vs Checkout Currency


WooCommerce supports one base currency per website. Most Indian merchants will utilize the INR base currency. To modify the base currency go to WooCommerce > Settings > General.


It is important to understand that modifying the base currency does not enable customers to pay in multiple currencies. If you wish to implement true multi-currency capability (i.e., customers can see prices in many different currencies and also checkout in their preferred currency) then you will need a multi-currency extension compatible with your payment processor. Changing the base currency also does not convert existing product price amounts.


Per[WooCommerce’s currency documentation](https://woocommerce.com/document/shop-currency/) , the Currency Converter widget merely alters how prices are viewed and does not convert the currency that the customer pays in. Therefore, if you want customers to buy from you in their home currency, then you will need to implement a multi-currency solution that enables them to complete the checkout process in their chosen currency.


**Setup Type** **What the Customer Views** **What Customers Pay**


Single-currency store Prices listed in the base currency of the store Base currency


Currency Converter widget Prices show for viewing purposes; base currency still paid Base currency


Multi-currency checkout Prices in the customer’s selected currency Customer selected currency, depending on gateway support


Before implementing a new currency option for foreign customers, verify whether your chosen payment gateway supports the new currency. If it does not, you may be required to either limit/block foreign currencies or locate an alternative method for processing payments in those currencies.


***Also read:[How to Integrate a Payment Gateway into Your Website](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/integrate-payment-gateway-india/)***


##


Set Up Your WooCommerce Store for International Payments


Create a clean staging/development version of your site before proceeding. Use sandbox mode and test credentials for simulated payments. As[WooCommerce’s test-order guidance](https://woocommerce.com/document/managing-orders/testing-orders/) explains, test orders can still trigger emails and appear in analytics, so isolate them from fulfilment and customer communications.


### Establish Your Base Currency


Next, navigate to WooCommerce > Settings > General. Establish the base currency of your store as INR. Verify the currency display (position), thousands separator, decimal separator and number of decimal digits. In most cases, an Indian merchant will list a price as follows: ₹1,499.00.


Ensure that pricing entered in USD has correct symbols for currencies, formats for decimals, and rounding rules for the intended customer demographic.


### Use a Compatible Multi-Currency Add-On


A multi-currency add-on should support the following features for customers to view and make purchases using currencies like[USD, EUR, GBP, AED or SGD](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/accept-business-payments-from-india/) , where supported:


- Support for selecting a currency
- Geolocation-based automatic currency detection, if needed
- Ability for customers to check out using their selected currency.
- Automatic updates of exchange rates
- Payment gateway compatibility
- Taxation, shipping costs, coupon redemption and refunds


##


Select a WooCommerce International Payment Gateway


Choose a gateway that supports all of the currencies, cards and payment types utilized by your consumers. Check whether the gateway can:


- Support sales into countries and currencies that you wish to support
- Accept international credit and debit cards
- Include the most well-known Indian payment options such as UPI and net banking
- Allow you to configure a test mode or offer sandbox credentials
- Manage partial refunds, webhooks and other events associated with processing orders
- Offer detailed[settlement and reconciliation reporting](https://www.cashfree.com/settlement-and-reconciliation-guide/)
- Comply with applicable Indian regulatory standards


Our[WooCommerce payment gateway plugin](https://www.cashfree.com/woocommerce-payment-gateway-india/) offers the ability to accept UPI, credit cards, debit cards, net banking, wallet transactions and Buy Now Pay Later options. Our[International Payment Gateway](https://www.cashfree.com/international-payment-gateway/) supports 140+ currencies, subject to payment-method availability and account configuration. Confirm compatibility with your specific multi-currency extension and plugin version before enabling foreign-currency checkout.


Before live use, enable international cards in our Merchant Dashboard under Settings > Payment Methods and complete the applicable activation requirements. An active domestic gateway alone does not establish international acceptance.


##


Configure Cashfree on Your WooCommerce Store


Configuring our payment gateway for an India-based company usually takes place in three steps: download/install our WooCommerce plugin, enable our payment gateway inside of WooCommerce, and add your correct API keys. Our[WooCommerce integration guide](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/checkout/woocommerce) covers the configuration.


### Step 1: Download and Install Our Plugin


1. Download our[official Cashfree plugin for WooCommerce](https://wordpress.org/plugins/cashfree/) .
2. Log in to WordPress.
3. Navigate to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin to add the new plugin.
4. Upload the plugin file.
5. Install and activate the plugin from the Plugins page.


Alternatively, manually copy the plugin directory into` /wp-content/plugins/` and then activate the plugin from the WordPress administrator area. Use one installation method.


### Step 2: Enable Our Gateway


1. Navigate to WooCommerce > Settings > Payments. Older versions may show Checkout instead.
2. Select “Cashfree” as a payment method and enable it.
3. Insert your App ID and Secret Key.
4. Toggle sandbox mode (necessary to perform testing)
5. Save your changes.


Production credentials only operate in live mode. Credentials for sandbox mode will only function while sandbox mode is enabled. Mixing environments and keys will cause authentication failures. Obtain the matching[Payment Gateway API keys](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/api-reference/authentication) from our Merchant Dashboard. Complete domain whitelisting under Developers > Whitelisting before live use.


##


How to Test International Payments on WooCommerce


Prior to making any test purchases, toggle the environment to test mode. Go to your test credentials located in your Cashfree Merchant Dashboard and select sandbox mode in the plugin. No real bank payment is processed in the sandbox. You can also explore our checkout flows in[Dev Studio](https://www.cashfree.com/devstudio) ; this does not replace testing your actual WooCommerce store.


### Complete a Test Purchase


Put items in your shopping cart and proceed through the checkout process. Utilize a test credit card number and the matching expiry, CVV and authentication details from our[sandbox test data](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/api-reference/payments/data-to-test-integration) . Verify that:


- The checkout process completed successfully.
- The currency chosen by the consumer during checkout was utilized as the currency for checkout.
- Shipping charges and taxes were appropriately applied for the order.
- The payment methods shown at checkout were available for the customer’s location and order currency.
- The payment updated the correct existing order within your WooCommerce store, without creating duplicate orders.
- The payment status correctly changed once completed.
- Automated confirmation email was sent to the customer upon completion of their purchase.
- Details of the order appeared within our test dashboard.


When any failure occurs in processing a payment via WooCommerce be sure to:


- Do not mark the order as paid in WooCommerce.
- Display a clear explanation of the failed payment to the customer.
- Provide an opportunity for customer to retry completing the purchase.


### Check Webhooks, Retries and Refunds


Complete the payment, then close the browser before returning to your store and check whether the order still receives its payment update. Review webhook delivery and ensure a failed or pending payment does not release goods or downloads.


If you have customised the integration, verify[webhook signatures](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/online/webhooks/signature-verification) before processing events. Check[duplicate-event handling](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/online/webhooks/webhook-indempotency) so repeated notifications do not trigger fulfilment twice. Use the plugin’s supported callback flow rather than creating a second fulfilment handler.


Test a full refund and a partial refund where supported. Match the original payment, refund reference, amount and currency in WooCommerce and our dashboard. Changing an order status or recording a manual refund does not by itself send money back to a card.


##


Test WooCommerce Multi-Currency Payments


Switch to another currency by acting like you are a customer.


### Test Currencies at Checkout


Place an item into the shopping cart using a single currency (e.g. USD), and go through the checkout process with that same currency. Verify that the payment method used by the gateway accepts the chosen currency and the amount invoiced is correct based on the total cost of the items in the order.


Repeat this check for each currency you intend to offer. Compare the product page, cart, WooCommerce order, gateway amount and currency, and confirmation email. Check shipping, taxes, coupons and rounding. Refresh the cart and retry payment to catch currency changes caused by sessions or caching.


### Validate WooCommerce Foreign Card Payments Before Going Live


Use our documented international/USD sandbox scenarios where supported. A domestic test card alone does not validate every foreign-card or currency combination. Our sandbox does not currently support PayPal or bank transfer payment modes.


After account activation and staging checks, arrange a low-value live foreign-card payment with an authorised tester using their own card. Live payments involve real funds and[applicable fees](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-gateway-charges/) . Check authentication, the WooCommerce order, the live dashboard, refund processing and the actual settlement record. Sandbox results cannot prove issuer approval or live FX and settlement behaviour.


***Also read:[How to Receive International Business Payments in India](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/how-to-receive-international-business-payments-in-india/)***


##


Conclusion


Before you start accepting international payments, you need to have completed a full test cycle on your India-based WooCommerce site. This includes testing all elements of customer experience such as selecting the desired currency for the purchase. Also test how customers can use international credit/debit cards to purchase from your website. Make sure all checkout steps work as intended. Check if proper errors are being handled while the user is checking out. Finally, test if all returns/refunds are working properly and that webhooks are delivering the expected payment and refund updates. Verify settlement separately after an approved live payment.

##


Frequently Asked Questions


#### Can my Indian WooCommerce store accept international payments?


Yes. As long as the payment gateway used by your Indian WooCommerce store accepts foreign credit/debit cards, offers international payment options, and your account has international acceptance enabled, your Indian WooCommerce store can accept international payments. Multi-currency checkout is optional.


#### What should I do to test international payments on my WooCommerce store?


To test international payments on your WooCommerce store, first enable “test” mode in your payment gateway. Then, using the test card numbers available via your payment gateway, create a test purchase. After completing the test purchase, confirm the status of the test purchase, confirm the currency was correctly applied to the test purchase, confirm the refund process worked properly, confirm your webhooks fired off properly, and then review your test transactions in your payment gateway’s dashboard.


#### Do I need a multi-currency option to accept international payments?


No. While having a multi-currency option would help your customers see prices in their local currencies and complete a purchase in their local currencies, you are still able to accept international payments via your primary store currency.
